title: Venera 4, 1967 — the probe built to float on Venus, with a lock made of sugar
sources: Wikipedia: Venera 4 — Soviet probe; in 1967 the first successful probe to analyse the environment of another planet in place, and the first spacecraft to survive entry into another planet's atmosphere; its capsule could float in case of a water landing, and its lock was made of sugar, meant to dissolve in liquid water and release the transmitter antennas; during entry the heat shield reached 11,000 °C and deceleration 300 g; the parachute opened at about 52 km; the atmosphere measured 90–93% carbon dioxide; at the end of a 26 km descent the temperature reached 262 °C and the pressure 22 atmospheres, and the signal ended; because of a radar altimeter ambiguity the Soviet team initially announced the probe had reached the surface, a claim quickly dismissed; the probes Venera 3–6 were not built to withstand the surface pressure; the first soft landing on Venus was Venera 7 in 1970
Wikipedia: Atmosphere of Venus — surface temperature about 467 °C and pressure about 93 bar
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1945 Juan Perón marries Eva Duarte; 1356 the Basel earthquake

post.facebook:
On this day in 1967, the Soviet probe Venera 4 reached Venus — and became the first spacecraft to analyse the atmosphere of another planet from inside it.

Nobody knew what lay beneath the clouds, so its capsule was built to float in case it came down in water. Its antenna lock was made of sugar, meant to dissolve in liquid water and free the antennas.

It hit the atmosphere so hard that its heat shield reached 11,000 °C. Then the parachute opened, and the probe began sending back the air of Venus: 90–93% carbon dioxide. As it fell, the temperature climbed to 262 °C and the pressure to 22 atmospheres — and the signal stopped.

The Soviet team first announced it had reached the surface; a radar quirk had fooled them, and the claim was quickly dropped. There was no water: at the ground, Venus is about 467 °C. Three years later, Venera 7 made the first landing.

Also on 18 October: Juan Perón married Eva Duarte (1945), and an earthquake destroyed Basel (1356).

youtube.description:
18 October 1967: Venera 4 reached Venus. Built to float in case it landed in water, its antenna lock was made of sugar, designed to dissolve. It survived an 11,000-degree entry, opened its parachute and became the first probe to measure another planet's atmosphere — almost all carbon dioxide. At 262 °C and 22 atmospheres, the signal stopped. Moscow first announced it had reached the surface — a radar quirk had fooled them. There was no water; Venus' surface is about 467 °C. Venera 7 landed three years later.

Also on 18 October: Perón marries Eva Duarte (1945) and the Basel earthquake (1356).
